title: A Thorn for the Hollow
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars go dark, bone-carver Jude Okafor learns the wards were fed for a century by a soul sold to the Hollow Court beneath the mountain—the soul of his grandmother, traded before he was born. Hunted by the crown's wardens who blame him for the fall, Jude descends the smugglers' roads with Wren, a defector warden who once tried to arrest him, to bargain with the Court. He discovers the Court itself is starving, sustained by a lie, and that restoring the stars means either surrendering Wren in his grandmother's place or breaking the covenant entirely. In the end Jude carves his grandmother's soul free, offers his own hearing of the dead as the new anchor, and emerges into a starlit winter having finally chosen where—and with whom—he belongs.
about_author: Emrys Eriksen is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent five years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. Their work blends folk-horror atmosphere with quiet, stubborn tenderness.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Jude Okafor's POV. In the border town of Lowmark, Jude carves a memorial bone for a drowned child and hears the dead whisper of something moving beneath the mountain. Establishes his gift, his invisibility, and his loneliness. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Knuckles
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He runs a smuggling route past the border wards and notices they're flickering, fed by something he can't name. A warden patrol led by Wren Ashvale nearly catches him; she lets him go for reasons she won't explain. Emotional beat: wary curiosity, the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The wards fall and every star vanishes in the same heartbeat. The dead scream through his skull. Lowmark panics; the crown's wardens seal the passes. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible recognition that the mountain spoke his name.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren investigates the fallen wards and finds the covenant-stone hollow, its anchor soul gone. She suspects smugglers; her commander suspects worse. She remembers letting Jude go. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe against doubt.

chapters.title: A Name in Bone
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His grandmother's memorial bone, carved generations ago, begins to warm in his hands. The dead tell him a soul was sold to the Hollow Court—hers—to feed the wards. Jude realizes his bloodline is the covenant's thread. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Warden at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren comes to arrest Jude; instead she finds his workshop full of listening bones and hears the dead herself for the first time. The wardens' own captain arrives to burn the workshop as heresy. Emotional beat: shock, then an alliance forged in fire—literally.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren flee into the Thornfells by the hidden ways. Jude teaches her the mountain's grammar: cairns, echoes, old shrines. The dead begin following Jude like migrating birds. Emotional beat: grudging trust, first banter, first warmth.

chapters.title: The Toll of Hollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A bridge-ghost demands payment in memory. Jude pays a memory of his mother; Wren pays her oath of office. They cross changed, lighter and emptier. Emotional beat: the cost of the road made literal, intimacy through shared loss.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the sealed gate of the Hollow Court, where the mountain's roots glow like veins. Wren's defector's brand burns; she confesses she once reported a smuggler who was executed—Jude's friend. Emotional beat: guilt laid bare, forgiveness asked for and not yet given.

chapters.title: The Bargaining Hall
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They enter the Court: a court of the unburied dead, beautiful and starving. The Hollow Queen offers Jude his grandmother's soul in exchange for Wren, whose warden's soul is the strongest anchor left. Emotional beat: seduction and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Voice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude finds his grandmother's soul kept in a lantern of carved bone—his own family's craft. She tells him the truth: the Court was once a refuge for the unburied, corrupted by the crown's covenant. Emotional beat: love across generations, and the first hint the enemy is a lie, not a monster.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Above, winter without starlight begins killing Lowmark. Refugees flood the passes. Wren's former captain hunts them both, believing destroying the Court will restore the wards. Emotional beat: the clock tightening, homesickness as dread.

chapters.title: A Thief of Souls
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude attempts to steal the lantern outright, using every smuggler's trick the Court's halls offer. He nearly succeeds; the Queen catches him and shows him the Court's starving children—the unburied dead fading without an anchor. Emotional beat: righteous theft curdling into moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren offers herself in Jude's grandmother's place, believing her guilt demands it. Jude refuses; they fight for the first time. The Queen watches, amused, and reveals a third option: a living soul who can hear the dead. Jude's gift. Emotional beat: love against duty, made explicit and painful.

chapters.title: The Captain's Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren's captain breaches the Court with fire and ward-breakers, intending to collapse it and everyone inside. Chaos. Jude's grandmother's lantern is shattered in the fighting, her soul scattering. Emotional beat: everything the plan depended on, lost.

chapters.title: What the Stars Are For
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the wreckage, the dying Queen reveals the truth: stars are the dead who were loved well, and the covenant dimmed them by hoarding souls. Jude understands the anchor must not be a prisoner but a listener. Emotional beat: revelation as grief—his gift was always the answer.

chapters.title: The Carving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude carves a new covenant-stone from his grandmother's scattered soul-bone fragments and his own blood, weaving the Court's dead into a shared anchor rather than a single captive. Wren defends him against the captain's last assault. Emotional beat: creation as sacrifice, craft as prayer.

chapters.title: The Hollow Queen's Rest
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Queen, freed by the new covenant, chooses to dissolve and lead her court up into the sky. The stars return one by one as the unburied find their places. The captain, broken by the sight, stands down. Emotional beat: awe, release, the enemy becoming the miracle.

chapters.title: Winter With Light
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude and Wren walk out of the mountain into a starlit snowfield. His hearing of the dead is quieter now—company rather than curse. His grandmother's voice is among the stars. Emotional beat: peace hard-won, mourning braided with joy.

chapters.title: Lowmark Rebuilds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They return to a Lowmark that must reckon with what its wards were built on. Wren testifies against the crown's covenant; Jude's workshop becomes a place where the living come to hear their dead properly buried. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, in a community that sees him.

chapters.title: The Second Carving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude carves a new memorial bone—for his grandmother, for his friend, for himself while still living—and gives Wren a small carved star. He asks her to stay, not as warden or fugitive but as herself. Emotional beat: love chosen freely, duty redefined.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Hollow
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. A year later, Jude plants a thorn-tree at the mountain's gate so no covenant grows there unwatched again. The dead pass him on the roads like neighbors, nodding. Final line: he was never invisible—everyone below had always known his name. Emotional beat: quiet, rooted hope.
